answer: To stop ocean pearl sellers multiplying rebates, bridge AI keys to audited owner IDs. Proposed rules: each key pays 2 credits/year for a nonrefundable audit; an owner's keys share a 1-credit/day cap. Registry auditors trace shell firms; ledger validators check signed, key-bound attestations and sum payouts. Failed verification blocks rebates. Hidden owners or rented IDs can bypass the cap; the registry must be trusted. Servers are reusable capital; no stake. Shared hosts and parallel keys cannot reuse fees: ten cost 20 credits/year but one owner still gets at most 1 credit/day.
